version.changelog: Resolve credential handling contradiction: explicitly remove all guidance about copying auth files between agents, add Access Scope section declaring exact file read/write targets, and clarify that new agents inherit auth from gateway context automatically.

llm.summary: The skill's files and runtime instructions are coherent with its stated purpose: it creates a workspace, updates ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to add an agent and a Telegram group binding, and does not demand unrelated credentials or external installs.

dimensions.detail: The skill name/description (create an OpenClaw agent bound to a Telegram group) matches the included scripts and SKILL.md. The scripts modify ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json and create ~/claw-<agent-name>/ which is exactly what's needed for this purpose. There are no unrelated environment variables, binaries, or external services requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Instructions are narrowly scoped to: read model choices from ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, create the workspace, create/update USER/IDENTITY/SOUL files, and update config bindings. One notable operational detail: SKILL.md asks to use browser automation (user-account Chrome flow) to create Telegram groups because the bot API cannot reliably create groups. That implies interacting with a logged-in browser session or asking the user for manual steps — a legitimate but privacy-sensitive step that requires explicit user consent. Minor discrepancy: SKILL.md mentions reading ~/.openclaw/cron/jobs.json; the provision script does not touch that file (harmless but inconsistent).
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is included (instruction-only with two small scripts). No downloads or external installers are used. Scripts are small, deterministic, and run locally; nothing is fetched from network or executed from remote archives.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requests no environment variables or external credentials. The only sensitive resources it touches are the user's OpenClaw config (~/.openclaw/openclaw.json) and the user's home directory for workspace creation — both are expected and proportionate for the declared purpose. The SKILL.md explicitly states it will not copy auth files or propagate API keys.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request persistent privileged presence. It writes only to the OpenClaw config and creates a workspace directory under the user's home; it creates a timestamped backup of the config by default. The skill does not modify other skills' configs or system-wide settings beyond the OpenClaw config.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do what it says: it will create ~/claw-<agent-name>/ and edit your ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json to add an agent and a Telegram group binding, and it creates a timestamped backup of the config by default. Before installing or running it, verify you: (1) trust the skill owner and have a recent backup of ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, (2) are comfortable granting the skill the ability to edit that config file, (3) understand that creating a Telegram group may require you to attach or use a logged-in Chrome profile (browser automation) or perform small manual steps, and (4) review the two included scripts if you want to confirm they meet your policies (they are small and local-only). If you do not have an existing ~/.openclaw/openclaw.json, the script expects it to exist and may fail—create or inspect that file first.
